smells.finding: gate_spec.py:signal_preservation_guard (lines 187-317, ~90 exec lines incl. the per-car-season loop body) computes field-relative values, then per group: trajectory residual, direct residual, accuracy_ok (with a stored-sigma vs fallback-scale branch), collapse detection, and a reason string -- five concerns folded into one loop body. Behavior is correct and well-tested; recommend extracting the accuracy_ok and collapse computations into two small named helpers (_accuracy_ok(...), _is_collapsed(...)) for a future gate, not blocking here since the logic is frozen-by-authority and tests pass.

gate_spec.py:paired_holdout_floor_per_car_season (lines 80-103) and model_holdout_spread_per_car_season (lines 106-122) share the identical 'dropna -> per-season count -> filter >=min_rows -> groupby(season_key)[col].std()' shape, differing only in whether a weekend_relative transform is applied first. A shared private helper (e.g. _trusted_season_std(df, col, season_key, min_rows)) would remove the duplication. Minor, non-blocking -- both functions are short, independently tested, and the duplication is unlikely to drift silently since floor.py's field_and_noise_stats already centralizes the primary x4 metric logic.

The pair (weekend_key, season_key) travels together as two separate parameters through nearly every function in floor.py and gate_spec.py (weekend_relative, field_and_noise_stats, per_axis_stats, floor_table, paired_holdout_floor_per_car_season, model_holdout_spread_per_car_season, fit_train_trajectory, signal_preservation_guard, evaluate_axis, evaluate_gate -- 10 call sites). A small NormalizationKeys(weekend_key, season_key) value object (defaulting to DEFAULT_WEEKEND_KEY/DEFAULT_SEASON_KEY) would collapse this to one parameter everywhere. Non-blocking for g1 (all call sites are internally consistent and tested), but worth doing before g2-g5 add more call sites on top.

Axis names (e.g. 'drag_area_closed_m2') are bare strings threaded through frame.AXES, floor.py, and gate_spec.py's model_cols: Mapping[str, str] with no enum/Literal type. Faithful to x4's own AXES list (a deliberate fidelity choice, not an oversight), but as g2-g5 fan this out further a Literal[...] alias or small Axis enum would catch a typo'd axis name at the type-check/lint boundary instead of a silent KeyError/empty-result at runtime. Low severity, non-blocking.

gate_spec.evaluate_gate takes 9 parameters (train_df, holdout_df, axes, model_cols, weekend_key, season_key, alpha, seed, beat_threshold); evaluate_axis takes 8. Mitigated by keyword defaults matching the frozen constants (only the first 4 of evaluate_gate are typically supplied), but a GateConfig dataclass bundling weekend_key/season_key/alpha/seed/beat_threshold (the same data-clump flagged above) would address both smells together. Non-blocking -- every call site in the tests already relies on the defaults, so this is a future-ergonomics note for g5's real integration, not a g1 defect.

override.repo_standard: g1-implementer-handoff.md Task section, floor.py bullet: 'a FAITHFUL re-implementation of x4's exact metric, parameterizable to run on ANY value column (not just raw), so later gates run it on the model's output' -- and the same handoff's Map Anchors: 'Capability: x4 weekend-relative floor metric reproduced as a reusable, column-parameterizable harness.'
override.reason: field_and_noise_stats' generality (arbitrary value_col/weekend_key/season_key rather than a raw-axis-only function) is not a guess at a future need -- it is a stated, near-term, explicitly authored requirement: g2-g5 (already planned, sequenced gates in the same launch order) will call this same function on model-output columns. Two concrete callers exist in this very diff already (per_axis_stats calling it on both the raw axis and its weekend_relative transform), and gate_spec.py's own paired_holdout_floor_per_car_season/model_holdout_spread_per_car_season are the second real, distinct caller shape -- so this clears the 'two adapters make a real seam' bar, not a one-off guess.
